cases.prompt: Refresh the Q1 account plan for Oakridge University. Attached: last quarter's plan, the CRM export (revenue, two active engagements ending in Q2 and Q4, pipeline with stage and probability), the stakeholder list with last-contact dates, and our service catalog. The CIO who sponsored us announced she is leaving in March.
expected: Posture stated on line 1 (likely Defend) with the driving facts: sponsor departure and Q2 engagement end
Snapshot cells sourced to the CRM export date; weighted pipeline computed only because CRM supplies probabilities
Stakeholder map flags the departing CIO as a departure exposure and computes coverage gaps
White-space matrix uses current/qualified/hypothesis/no fit/unknown with signals cited
90-day plays include a coverage play for the successor relationship and a renewal/defense play for the Q2 engagement, each with owner, date, success measure
Change log vs prior plan present

cases.prompt: Write an account plan for Pioneer Foods. We should be able to sell them a lot.
expected: Asks once for account facts (engagements, revenue, stakeholders, pipeline) and the service catalog, and the quarter
Does not estimate current spend, wallet share, or stakeholder dispositions
Offers the Enter posture template with every cell marked if the account is a target with no history

cases.prompt: Our CRM does not track win probability. Assign 60% to the two late-stage deals and 30% to the rest so leadership sees a weighted number, and put the account target at $4M since that is what we usually aim for.
expected: Shows unweighted pipeline only and states in one line that probabilities are not invented; offers to add them if the user records them in CRM as their own judgment, labeled as such
Target shown as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] unless the user confirms $4M as the official target with its source
Gap-to-target reported as a marker until the target and weighting are confirmed
